abstract: We study the rank-ten K3-type cohomology of even double covers of type-$(1,3)$ abelian surfaces and construct actual abelian sources on its Gaussian locus. The full anti-invariant double-Kummer lattice is $U^2\oplus D_{12}(-1)$; six exceptional differences saturate to a primitive $D_6(-1)$ with complement $U^2\oplus D_6(-1)$. We prove period rank eight. Assuming precisely Lemma 5.5 and Theorem 6.1 of OpenAI's September 30, 2026 quadratic-locus preprint, boundary and gluing calculations give algebraic comparisons with Picard-twelve K3 surfaces, with similarity multiplier two. Independently, a classical isotrivial K3 is dominated by a Gaussian elliptic curve times a genus-seven cyclic curve with Prym fivefold $P$. Hermitian classification, rational unitary density and K3 isogeny theorems transport this source and give Chow motives of abelian type. An explicit uniruled quotient of $E_i\times G\times G$ supplies an algebraic correspondence for the missing spin tenfold. An explicit cubic-surface line curve, incidence projector and cylinder identify this tenfold on a nonempty open. A compact-type specialization of Schoen's balanced Prym cycles supplies the mixed determinant classes on $P\times E_i^3$. Invariant theory first proves ordinary Hodge conjectures and the specified Kuga–Satake tensors at the full unitary group. Relative specialization of that fixed tensor, together with existing K3 and Kuga–Satake Hodge theorems, extends ordinary mixed Hodge conjectures to every smooth Gaussian source. Fully twisted sources and a rectangular-partition construction in the complete spin representation prove generalized Hodge conjectures, including at Hodge-group drops. A direct Prym period calculation and odd-rank Hermitian scaling extend the abelian conclusions to every Gaussian fivefold of signature $(1,4)$, including endomorphism and Picard jumps. Reproducible CPU calculations verify finite lattice, branch and character identities. Arbitrary tuples of unrelated special sources and the generic orthogonal deformation remain outside the argument; the general rational Hodge conjecture remains open.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Adds the coherent Gaussian extension in Section 10 and Appendix B: an actual algebraic tenfold source from the quotient of E_i times two cyclic curves, an explicit cubic-surface line curve and incidence cylinder, Schoen determinant specialization, ordinary and generalized Hodge conjectures for the associated mixed Gaussian products, and the prescribed Kuga–Satake tensors, including smooth special points. Adds the direct Prym period calculation and odd-rank Hermitian transport to all signature-(1,4) Gaussian fivefolds. Addresses the v1 review by citing Nori's Gaussian elliptic-product domination via van Geemen Example 11.3 and explicitly describing arbitrary-period transport as existential, without a branch-recovery algorithm. Retains the conditional labels on the imported rank-ten comparison and excludes the generic orthogonal deformation. The new smooth-carrier/deformation experiments are not part of this revision.
